examples.scenario: Window xoff=10,xsize=5 includes column 15.
examples.reason: The covered columns are 10..14; xoff+xsize is the exclusive stop.

examples.scenario: Window yoff=20,ysize=3 includes row 23.
examples.reason: The covered rows are 20..22; yoff+ysize is exclusive.

examples.scenario: NumPy slice uses arr[y0:y1+1,x0:x1+1] after y1/x1 were already exclusive stops.
examples.reason: Adding one creates an off-by-one source window.

examples.scenario: A negative row index is allowed to wrap to the raster bottom.
examples.reason: Target raster addresses must fail bounds checks rather than use Python negative indexing.

examples.scenario: np.take mode=clip is used for a column outside raster width.
examples.reason: Clipping silently substitutes an edge cell for an invalid address.

examples.scenario: np.take mode=wrap is used for an out-of-range row.
examples.reason: Wrapping changes the geographic cell identity.

examples.scenario: ravel_multi_index mode=clip converts an invalid row to the last row.
examples.reason: Flat cell identity must raise on invalid coordinates.

examples.scenario: Source window width is 100 but buffer width is 50.
examples.reason: RasterIO may decimate when source and buffer sizes differ.

examples.scenario: Source window is 50x50 but output buffer is 100x100.
examples.reason: Upsampling is derived processing, not native cell extraction.

examples.scenario: ReadAsArray uses a narrower buffer datatype while extracting the exact window.
examples.reason: Window identity requires source precision to be preserved.

examples.scenario: A floating xoff=10.4 is silently truncated to 10.
examples.reason: Floating and integer source-window semantics must be explicitly reconciled.

examples.scenario: Floating source-window validity is enabled but dfXSize/dfYSize are not recorded.
examples.reason: All precise window parameters are part of replay identity.

examples.scenario: GDAL 3.10 and 3.11 produce different -projwin source windows and version is ignored.
examples.reason: GDAL 3.11 changed how transformed projwin extents select source windows.

examples.scenario: Nearest-neighbour -projwin expansion to pixel boundaries is not recorded.
examples.reason: Expansion can change included source cells.

examples.scenario: -projwin_srs is described as raster reprojection.
examples.reason: It changes window-coordinate interpretation, not the dataset CRS.

examples.scenario: A -srcwin partly outside the raster is accepted with zero-filled cells.
examples.reason: Terminal sampling should use an explicit outside-source error policy.

examples.scenario: A completely outside source window returns nodata and is treated as a valid empty parcel.
examples.reason: Invalid addressing must not become a business result.

examples.scenario: Raster clip bbox expands to pixel boundaries but the expanded bounds are not logged.
examples.reason: The actual included cells are defined by the expanded whole-pixel window.

examples.scenario: VRT SrcRect is 100x100 and DstRect is 50x50 but values are called native.
examples.reason: Different source/destination rectangle sizes imply derived mapping.

examples.scenario: VRT contributing source changes while output window pixels happen to match.
examples.reason: Equal output does not prove the same native source lineage.

examples.scenario: A right-edge GDAL block is treated as full nominal block width.
examples.reason: Only GetActualBlockSize valid pixels may enter the window.

examples.scenario: A bottom-edge block contributes padded rows beyond raster height.
examples.reason: Padded block storage is not valid raster content.

examples.scenario: Block-local column 7 is recorded without adding the block global x origin.
examples.reason: Terminal cell identity requires global raster row/column.

examples.scenario: Window pixel count differs from xsize*ysize.
examples.reason: The extracted native window must contain exactly the declared number of cells before masks.

examples.scenario: NumPy slice shape differs from declared GDAL window dimensions.
examples.reason: Half-open slice and GDAL window must describe the same cells.

examples.scenario: BBox-only filter is treated as the exact parcel raster window.
examples.reason: BBox may define a read window but not exact polygon membership.

examples.scenario: A mosaic-derived window index is reused as a native source-tile index.
examples.reason: Derived grid origins/resolutions can differ from source tile addressing.

examples.scenario: Stack target-aligned output indices are treated as original raster indices.
examples.reason: Target alignment creates output-grid coordinates, not source identity.

examples.scenario: Reproject source-contribution rectangle is reported as an exact native target window.
examples.reason: Warp source regions are derived interpolation support areas.

examples.scenario: gdal raster pixel-info reports a row/col different from primary address and discrepancy is ignored.
examples.reason: Independent address channels must agree.

examples.scenario: as-features row/col differs from extracted-window cell IDs.
examples.reason: Independent cell enumeration must reconcile.

examples.scenario: Golden extracted window matches pixels but width differs.
examples.reason: Pixel sequence without identical shape does not prove the same window.

examples.scenario: Golden window matches shape but geotransform differs.
examples.reason: Same array values can refer to different ground locations.

examples.scenario: Golden comparison matches metadata but one pixel differs.
examples.reason: Exact window replay requires identical native pixel content.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent window digests match but cell-id-set digests differ.
examples.reason: A byte-equivalent buffer can still be associated with the wrong global addresses if provenance is wrong.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent cell sets match but source-window parameter digests differ.
examples.reason: Accidental same-cell output does not erase execution-policy drift.

examples.scenario: Raster dimensions changed between manifest creation and runtime read.
examples.reason: Bounds must be validated against the exact runtime raster identity.

examples.scenario: Window xsize or ysize is zero and processing continues.
examples.reason: An empty native window is not a valid terrain sampling result unless explicitly expected by contract.

examples.scenario: Window xsize/ysize is derived from rounded geospatial extent without recording rounding.
examples.reason: Rounding policy controls included cells.

examples.scenario: Rasterize output extent/size is substituted for native DTM source-window bounds.
examples.reason: Rasterization creates a new target grid.

examples.scenario: A fixture proves half-open logic and its window is copied to the target parcel.
examples.reason: Examples validate logic only; target window needs canonical runtime binding.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution conditions remain BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second source-window runner is launched while shared runner ACK is absent.
examples.reason: Continuation contract requires the existing single shared runner.

examples.scenario: Source-window preparation is reported as an actual parcel elevation.
examples.reason: No target raster sampling has executed.

examples.scenario: A 99.99 readiness score is reported as pixel-window measurement accuracy.
examples.reason: Readiness is validation preparation, not a measured geospatial accuracy statistic.

examples.scenario: Batch 80 is reported as final height-difference output.
examples.reason: Canonical point, exact boundary, immutable DTM binding and runtime extraction are still required.
